newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Pet food wars hit Dalgety profits.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Pet food wars hit Dalgety profits.

text.p: Tough competition over pet food could take a large bite out of British food and agribusiness Dalgety Plc's year profits due on September 16, and expectations of a fall in results are keeping share prices near year-lows.
"Everyone is expecting poor results. We think they have got it all to do at the moment," said one sector analyst who asked not to be named.

Forecasts are for pretax, pre-exceptional profits to fall to 90-104 million stg compared with 127 million stg previously, while the company is expected to sustain a total dividend of 22 to 22.5 pence, little changed from 22.0 pence a year ago.
Exceptional charges of upwards of 60 million stg are expected.
"They signalled the dividend should be maintained. That has been an important prop to the share price. Without that it would be lower still," the analyst said.
Dalgety's shares were trading up one pence at 325-1/2 pence at 1055 GMT, just a whisker away from a year-low of 322 pence.
Dalgety is trying to integrate the pet food business that it gained when it bought the European business of U.S.-based Quaker Oats for 422 million stg just over a year ago.
It has seen market share eroded as competitors take advantage of its preoccupations, analysts said.
"The competition has attacked at a time when they knew Dalgety had its hands full," the analyst said.
Then earlier this year, Dalgety had to recall pet food in the Netherlands after 328 cats died, denting consumer confidence in the brand, analysts said.
Pet food accounts for around 40 percent of the company's operating profits, making it "critically important" to be successful here, one analyst said.
Dalgety produces Spillers branded pet foods and acquired the Felix and Fido lines when it bought the Quaker business.
Consumer fears over bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) have also affected the company, although it said in June costs relating to the BSE scare would not be over 25 million stg.
"The big question is how optimistic is Dalgety, does it think it can turn it round this year?" the analyst said.
"If they say in the statement things are still looking tough, then everyone will be very wary," he added.
